theses.title: AI power infrastructure bottleneck
theses.coreClaim: AI data-center growth is creating durable demand for grid, electrical, power-services, and behind-the-meter infrastructure providers.
theses.whyItMightCompound: Capacity bottlenecks can persist for years, pushing spend toward scarce engineering, construction, power-equipment, and specialized energy assets.
whatMustBeTrue: AI compute demand remains power-constrained rather than model-demand constrained.
Utilities, hyperscalers, and industrial customers continue funding grid and power upgrades.
Selected companies can convert demand into margin and backlog without severe execution or valuation risk.
invalidators: AI infrastructure demand slows materially or power intensity falls faster than expected.
Valuations price in most of the bottleneck upside.
Permitting, grid interconnect, or supply-chain limits prevent revenue conversion.
theses.convictionWhy: Multiple existing notes point to AI power bottlenecks, but asset-specific valuation and competitive positioning still need work.

theses.title: Critical materials and defense infrastructure
theses.coreClaim: Supply-chain resilience, rearmament, nuclear fuel, drones, aerospace components, and critical materials may support durable investment themes.
theses.whyItMightCompound: Geopolitical fragmentation and industrial policy can create long-lived demand for constrained domestic/allied capacity.
whatMustBeTrue: Defense and resilience spending remains structurally elevated.
Chosen companies have defensible niches rather than commodity exposure only.
Valuation leaves room for multi-year compounding.
invalidators: Spending normalizes or political support fades.
Theme is too broad to create investable edge.
Best assets are already priced for perfection.
theses.convictionWhy: Original broad theme has been split into more explicit active-owned theses: rearmament/aerospace-defense and strategic commodity stockpiling/critical minerals.

theses.title: Rearmament and aerospace/defense capacity
theses.coreClaim: Western/allied rearmament, geopolitical fragmentation, drone/missile demand, and defense-industrial capacity constraints create a durable long-horizon tailwind for aerospace and defense exposure.
theses.whyItMightCompound: Defense spending may remain structurally elevated for years while supply chains, munitions, aerospace components, and prime/subcontractor capacity remain constrained.
whatMustBeTrue: Rearmament remains a multi-year budget priority across the US and allies.
Defense/aerospace suppliers can convert budget growth into revenue, backlog, and margins.
ETF exposure is a better or sufficiently diversified expression versus selecting only primes/subcontractors.
invalidators: Defense budget growth stalls or political support fades.
Valuations fully price in rearmament without enough earnings conversion.
Program execution, cost overruns, or procurement bottlenecks prevent revenue/margin capture.
theses.convictionWhy: Alex explicitly identified XAR as one of his highest-conviction holdings, with rearmament as the thesis.

theses.title: Energy demand growth and infrastructure toll booths
theses.coreClaim: Energy demand growth, energy security, and infrastructure constraints support owning both upstream/sector energy exposure and midstream/toll-booth infrastructure.
theses.whyItMightCompound: Higher/steadier energy demand can support cash flows across energy producers and midstream infrastructure; toll-booth assets may benefit from volumes and scarcity without requiring perfect commodity-price timing.
whatMustBeTrue: Energy demand remains resilient or grows despite transition narratives.
Midstream/energy infrastructure retains pricing power and cash-flow durability.
Portfolio needs an energy/inflation/geopolitical hedge sleeve alongside growth theses.
invalidators: Energy demand structurally weakens or supply overwhelms demand for a prolonged period.
Regulatory/tax/political changes impair midstream economics or distributions.
Position becomes too commodity-cycle exposed relative to desired portfolio role.
theses.convictionWhy: Alex explicitly identified XLE and MLPX as high-conviction holdings tied to energy demand growth and “own the toll booths.”

theses.title: Strategic commodity stockpiling and critical minerals
theses.coreClaim: Sovereign stockpiling, resource nationalism, supply-chain security, and critical-mineral scarcity create durable demand for rare earths, strategic metals, and upstream natural-resource exposure.
theses.whyItMightCompound: Governments and industrial buyers may increasingly prioritize security of supply over lowest-cost just-in-time sourcing, supporting constrained producers and resource-linked assets.
whatMustBeTrue: Sovereign/strategic stockpiling becomes a persistent policy response to geopolitical fragmentation.
Critical minerals and upstream resources remain supply-constrained or strategically scarce.
ETF baskets provide adequate exposure despite commodity cyclicality and jurisdiction/company quality dispersion.
invalidators: Stockpiling proves temporary or politically overstated.
New supply, substitution, or demand weakness overwhelms scarcity thesis.
ETF composition is too low-quality/cyclical to capture the strategic-stockpiling thesis cleanly.
theses.convictionWhy: Alex explicitly identified REMX and GUNR as high-conviction holdings tied to critical minerals and strategic commodity stockpiling by sovereigns.

theses.title: Macro security and real-assets pillar
theses.coreClaim: Geopolitical fragmentation, rearmament, energy demand growth, infrastructure scarcity, and sovereign strategic stockpiling are core pillars of Alex’s macro outlook and justify a deliberate portfolio sleeve across defense, energy infrastructure, and critical/natural resources.
theses.whyItMightCompound: If the world is shifting from cheap/globalized abundance toward security-of-supply, reindustrialization, rearmament, and resource constraints, then defense capacity, energy toll booths, and critical materials can remain structurally supported over a 5–10 year horizon.
whatMustBeTrue: Rearmament and defense-industrial spending remain structurally elevated.
Energy demand and infrastructure constraints persist despite transition narratives.
Sovereigns and strategic buyers increasingly stockpile critical commodities/minerals.
Portfolio expressions capture the macro pillar without excessive duplication, cyclicality, or valuation risk.
invalidators: Geopolitical/security spending normalizes faster than expected.
Energy demand or infrastructure cash-flow assumptions weaken materially.
Critical-mineral/stockpiling demand proves temporary or ETF composition fails to capture it.
The sleeve becomes too large/correlated relative to other portfolio bets.
theses.convictionWhy: Alex explicitly confirmed this combined geopolitical/security + real-assets complex is a core pillar of his macro outlook.
theses.currentExposure: Core mapped holdings 13.08%; broader adjacent exposure 30.87% of portfolio as of 2026-05-13T01:38:39.082Z.

theses.title: Japanese financial reflation
theses.coreClaim: Japan rate normalization, wage/inflation reflation, governance reform, buybacks, and improved shareholder returns can lift megabank ROE and narrow the Japan bank discount.
theses.whyItMightCompound: Large Japanese banks have leverage to higher domestic rates/net interest income while retaining global/diversified franchises; sustained positive nominal growth could support multi-year earnings and capital-return upgrades.
whatMustBeTrue: BOJ policy stays on a gradual normalization path rather than returning to effective zero-rate stagnation.
Wages/inflation/nominal GDP remain strong enough to support loan demand and NIM without major credit losses.
MUFG/SMFG convert higher earnings into ROE improvement, dividends, buybacks, and valuation support.
invalidators: BOJ returns to effective zero-rate posture or rate hikes reverse quickly.
Credit losses or JGB/market losses overwhelm NIM benefits.
Shareholder returns disappoint and ROE fails to improve despite higher rates.
Yen/FX or global exposure undermines the reflation thesis.
theses.convictionWhy: Thesis is structurally plausible and differentiated, but current entries are not compelling enough for automatic accumulation; needs ongoing ROE/book-value and BOJ-rate monitoring.
theses.currentAction: approved-watchlist; wait for starter/attractive valuation ranges

theses.title: Optical networking and AI bandwidth bottleneck
theses.coreClaim: AI infrastructure demand shifts bottlenecks from compute alone to high-bandwidth optical transport, data-center interconnect, fiber, photonics, and physical connectivity between GPUs, racks, campuses, and regions.
theses.whyItMightCompound: If AI clusters keep scaling, hyperscalers and carriers may need years of optical/fiber upgrades. CIEN is the purer coherent optical networking expression; GLW is broader physical-layer fiber/connectivity exposure.
whatMustBeTrue: AI training/inference growth keeps optical bandwidth and interconnect demand structurally tight.
Hyperscaler/carrier capex translates into durable revenue/backlog rather than a one-time inventory cycle.
CIEN/GLW defend margins and relevance as architectures move toward higher-speed/co-packaged optics and denser fiber systems.
invalidators: Hyperscaler AI capex slows materially or shifts away from external optical intensity.
Orders prove to be inventory/channel pull-forward rather than durable demand.
Competition, pricing pressure, or architecture shifts compress margins and reduce vendor capture.
Valuation remains too stretched relative to forward growth.
theses.convictionWhy: Thesis quality is strong and differentiated, but both CIEN and GLW currently screen stretched; keep on watchlist and emphasize patience/not chasing.
theses.currentAction: stretched-wait; notify only on meaningful pullbacks into starter/attractive ranges

theses.title: Medical tools and specialty device compounders
theses.coreClaim: High-quality healthcare tools and specialty medtech franchises can compound outside the dominant macro/AI/security sleeves, adding a durable quality-growth ballast if valuation and execution remain disciplined.
theses.whyItMightCompound: DHR benefits from life-science tools/bioprocessing recovery and recurring consumables; BSX benefits from specialty device product cycles such as electrophysiology, Watchman, and pulsed-field ablation.
whatMustBeTrue: Bioprocessing/life-science demand normalizes and Danaher converts recovery into operating leverage.
Boston Scientific sustains product-cycle growth without major share loss, reimbursement pressure, or safety issues.
Healthcare quality exposure improves portfolio balance rather than becoming another low-conviction sprawl sleeve.
invalidators: DHR bioprocessing recovery stalls, lab budgets weaken, or M&A dilutes quality.
BSX FARAPULSE/Watchman growth disappoints, share losses accelerate, or guidance cuts persist.
Either name rerates without earnings support or no longer offers attractive risk/reward versus higher-conviction theses.
theses.convictionWhy: Good portfolio-diversifying quality-compounder candidate. DHR looks closest to actionable on current valuation; BSX needs quote/data verification and thesis-specific monitoring.
theses.currentAction: approved-watchlist; DHR possible starter if portfolio room exists; verify BSX quote before action

investingTaxonomyDecisionSheet.approvalPrompt: Approve/edit by cluster; then encode into thesis-taxonomy-decisions.json, regenerate thesis universe and governance audit, and prepare proposed app-side canonical changes for review.

investingTaxonomyDecisionWorkflow.purpose: Interactive Phase 2 taxonomy decision workflow for Alphalpha dashboard. Makes each decision point explicit with recommendation, why, consequences, affected allocation/assets, and staged-choice options.
decisionPrinciples: Make taxonomy decisions before rebalance decisions.
Every holding should have one primary classification for allocation math and optional secondary exposure tags for overlap.
Theses are conviction/evidence ranked; sleeves are portfolio-construction policies and should not compete in thesis conviction ranking.
Supabase/Thesis Baskets remains canonical; dashboard choices stage proposals for review rather than directly mutating canonical state.

decisionPoints.title: Approve canonical item kinds
decisionPoints.question: Should the canonical taxonomy distinguish thesis, sleeve, watchlist thesis, legacy/archive, and meta tag?
decisionPoints.recommendation: Approve these five kinds as first-class taxonomy categories in one canonical system.
decisionPoints.why: This prevents thesis baskets and portfolio construction roles from competing in one fake conviction ranking while still keeping one source of truth. Cash, broad beta, and quality ballast need governance, but they are not evidence-driven theses in the same sense as power scarcity or defense rearmament.

options.label: Approve kinds
options.meaning: Use thesis/sleeve/watchlist/legacy/meta as canonical kinds.

options.label: Single basket kind only
options.meaning: Treat every category as a basket; simpler but risks confusing sleeves with theses.

options.label: Revise kinds
options.meaning: Keep distinction but edit names/definitions.

consequences: If approved, sleeves get policy ranges rather than conviction scores.
Rebalance math can become mutually exclusive by primary classification.
Thesis conviction rankings become cleaner and less distorted by cash/beta/ballast positions.

decisionPoints.title: Consolidate AI compute / platforms / physical infrastructure
decisionPoints.question: Should paused AI Physical Infrastructure and derived AI platforms/compute/semis become one canonical AI compute + physical infrastructure thesis?
decisionPoints.recommendation: Yes — consolidate into one app-reviewed thesis, separate from power scarcity.
decisionPoints.why: The current split creates a paused canonical basket with meaningful secondary exposure and a noncanonical portfolio bucket with ~10% primary exposure. The assets share a compute/data-center/platform supply-chain driver, but that driver is distinct from electrical grid scarcity.

options.label: Consolidate
options.meaning: Create one AI compute + physical infrastructure thesis; retire the old split.

options.label: Keep split
options.meaning: Leave AI Physical Infrastructure paused and AI platforms as a separate derived bucket.

options.label: Fold into power
options.meaning: Treat AI compute mostly as driver of power scarcity; not recommended.

consequences: Clarifies that AMZN/GOOGL/MU/etc. are not power-scarcity assets even if AI load drives power demand.
Requires app-reviewed conviction and target range before any add/trim authority.
Reduces duplicate AI infrastructure categories.

decisionPoints.title: Classify nuclear power
decisionPoints.question: Should Nuclear Power be a standalone active thesis or a secondary tag/sub-thesis across power and resource security?
decisionPoints.recommendation: Use Nuclear Power as a secondary sub-thesis/tag for now, not a standalone primary basket, unless you want a dedicated nuclear allocation target.
decisionPoints.why: Nuclear exposure splits into different drivers: generation/services validate power scarcity, while uranium/fuel-cycle behaves like upstream resource security. A standalone basket risks double-counting unless it has its own target and asset boundary.

options.label: Secondary tag/sub-thesis
options.meaning: Use nuclear to tag power and uranium/resource holdings without separate primary allocation.

options.label: Standalone thesis
options.meaning: Create/keep a separate active nuclear thesis with its own target and split asset rules.

options.label: Fold into power only
options.meaning: Treat nuclear primarily as power-generation expression.

consequences: Secondary-tag choice avoids double-counting uranium/resource exposure as both nuclear and critical materials.
Standalone choice requires target/min/max and a clean generation-vs-fuel boundary.
This affects how underallocation to power is interpreted.

decisionPoints.title: Narrow critical materials / resource security
decisionPoints.question: Should Critical Materials stay broad or be narrowed/split into cleaner resource-security sub-theses?
decisionPoints.recommendation: Narrow it into Resource Security / Strategic Materials and explicitly exclude precious metals, broad commodities, and ag unless separately approved.
decisionPoints.why: The current bucket mixes copper, rare earths, uranium, ag commodities, broad materials ETFs, and natural resources. It also has conflicting conviction sources: app/digest low/falling while OpenClaw/portfolio review high. A narrower definition is required before target gaps mean anything.

options.label: Narrow
options.meaning: Keep one strategic materials thesis with stricter owns/does-not-own rules.

options.label: Split
options.meaning: Create separate copper/rare earths/uranium/ag theses.

options.label: Keep broad
options.meaning: Keep current broad bucket; simplest but least precise.

consequences: Makes the 10% target interpretable by excluding unrelated commodity/hedge exposures.
Forces separate treatment of uranium/fuel-cycle and ag commodities.
Prevents broad commodity ETFs from silently inflating strategic-materials exposure.

decisionPoints.title: Score precious metals as hedge vs alpha thesis
decisionPoints.question: Should Precious Metals be treated as a normal alpha thesis or a hedge/insurance thesis with separate scoring?
decisionPoints.recommendation: Keep it separate as a hedge/insurance thesis with a policy range and hedge-need score, not directly comparable to alpha thesis conviction.
decisionPoints.why: Precious metals may be held for insurance even when fresh alpha evidence is weak. Ranking it directly against power or defense by conviction can overstate trim pressure or understate its portfolio role. But it still needs a target/range so the hedge does not sprawl.

options.label: Hedge thesis
options.meaning: Use a policy range and hedge-need score separate from alpha conviction.

options.label: Normal thesis
options.meaning: Rank against all active theses by evidence conviction.

options.label: Sleeve
options.meaning: Treat as portfolio construction/insurance sleeve rather than thesis.

consequences: Avoids comparing insurance allocation one-for-one against growth/scarcity theses.
Still requires a canonical min/max or target range before rebalance recommendations.
Clarifies why low fresh-evidence conviction does not automatically equal sell.

decisionPoints.title: Archive or demote ag/Hormuz
decisionPoints.question: Should Agricultural Commodities Boom Downstream of Hormuz remain an active basket?
decisionPoints.recommendation: Archive or demote to low-priority watchlist unless you explicitly want durable ag/food-security exposure.
decisionPoints.why: The thesis appears second-order/stale and should not inflate critical-materials/resource-security allocation. It can remain as a monitored tail-risk idea without active allocation authority.

options.label: Archive/watchlist
options.meaning: Remove active allocation authority; keep evidence/history.

options.label: Keep active
options.meaning: Maintain as active thesis with boundary and target.

options.label: Fold into resources
options.meaning: Treat ag as part of resource security; not recommended without stronger thesis.

consequences: Reduces thesis sprawl.
Keeps ag as optional research without contaminating active resource-security exposure.
If kept active, needs separate target and validators.

decisionPoints.title: Convert Doomberg Energy View to evidence source
decisionPoints.question: Should Doomberg’s Energy View remain an allocation basket?
decisionPoints.recommendation: No — archive it as a legacy/evidence source and keep one active Energy demand/security + infrastructure tollbooths thesis.
decisionPoints.why: It duplicates the energy thesis but has no clear independent allocation boundary. Doomberg can remain an input/source tag without acting as a separate basket that competes for capital.

options.label: Archive as evidence
options.meaning: No separate allocation authority; evidence feeds energy thesis.

options.label: Keep active
options.meaning: Maintain separate basket with distinct boundary and target.

options.label: Merge
options.meaning: Absorb assets/history into energy thesis and retire separate basket.

consequences: Simplifies energy taxonomy.
Requires deciding whether energy target should split upstream vs midstream.
Preserves source history without duplicate allocation math.

decisionPoints.title: Energy target: one range or upstream/midstream ranges
decisionPoints.question: Should energy use one target range or separate upstream and midstream/tollbooth sub-ranges?
decisionPoints.recommendation: Use one thesis with secondary tags and optional sub-ranges for upstream beta vs midstream tollbooths.
decisionPoints.why: Alex’s stated conviction includes energy demand and owning tollbooths, but upstream and midstream have different drawdown/valuation profiles. One thesis avoids sprawl; sub-tags preserve risk control.

options.label: One thesis + sub-ranges
options.meaning: Single energy thesis with upstream/midstream tags and optional limits.

options.label: Separate theses
options.meaning: Split upstream energy and midstream tollbooths into distinct baskets.

options.label: Single range only
options.meaning: Simpler but hides risk differences.

consequences: Avoids over-fragmenting the energy thesis.
Allows midstream/tollbooth exposure to be treated differently from commodity beta.
Requires app target review because current 5% target does not match actual exposure.

decisionPoints.title: Classify quality/income ballast
decisionPoints.question: Should quality/income be a real thesis or a portfolio sleeve?
decisionPoints.recommendation: Treat it as a sleeve by default, with permission for individual holdings to graduate into separate theses later.
decisionPoints.why: The current group functions as stability/income/quality ballast. That is valuable, but it is not one coherent falsifiable thesis like power scarcity. It needs a policy range, not conviction ranking.

options.label: Sleeve
options.meaning: Quality/income gets policy range and portfolio role.

options.label: Thesis
options.meaning: Treat quality/income as evidence-ranked alpha thesis.

options.label: Split
options.meaning: Separate dividend ballast, quality compounders, and REIT/income.

consequences: Removes quality/income from thesis conviction rankings.
Enables policy-range review instead of false evidence score.
Some assets can later move to individual theses if warranted.

decisionPoints.question: Should cash/bonds and broad allocation ETFs become sleeves rather than theses?

decisionPoints.title: Set speculative sandbox treatment
decisionPoints.question: Should speculative small positions become a capped sleeve?
decisionPoints.recommendation: Yes — create a speculative sandbox sleeve with a small max cap and cleanup cadence.
decisionPoints.why: Small experiments can be useful, but without a cap they become thesis sprawl. A sleeve lets them exist without pretending each is an approved long-horizon thesis.
